original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For each fixed finite characteristic c>=3, construct full-coefficient unsigned connector words with c reads per row and Theta(c^(n/c)) optimal overhead above c(c^n-1).
scope_change_reason: The operation alphabet stays fixed. The demand is all nonzero coefficient rows in (Z/cZ)^n, extending the full ternary demand of PR4238/4244 to arbitrary n and finite characteristic. This is a local combinatorial side result rather than a supplier extension.
bottleneck_link: Full coefficient demand has a sharp overhead exponent in the complete-call model. This supplies an explicit abstract budget, but no actual consumer or physical admission is identified.
stop_rule: Stop at a proved overhead exponent with bounded literal checks; do not optimize a physical supplier without a caller and full invoice.
evidence: README.md gives the all-size cycle construction and all-word lower bound. verify.py emits 41 words and checks 36996 rows, 186532 calls, 28 cycles, 780 partitions, 2220 multisets, 12 dense cases and 6 controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the optimal leading constant in the excess above c(c^n-1), first for c=3 and n divisible by three?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The counting bound and block construction have the same exponent but different constants.
open_questions.first_step: Find smaller c-fold additive boundary bases and charge their positive-step realization and restoration.
open_questions.blocked_by: Abstract additive bases need not be cheaply realizable as restored source paths.

open_questions.question: Can the seven-source full ternary upper bound 6603 be lowered toward the cited 6588 lower bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the first unsettled size after the exact six-source predecessor.
open_questions.first_step: Search a short restored source path covering all 2186 nonzero rows by triple sums.
open_questions.blocked_by: Triple coverage and the full chronological path invoice must both hold.

open_questions.question: Which real caller needs full coefficient demand at favorable complete physical prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A complete-call word alone is not a supplier.
open_questions.first_step: Pin one caller and its maps, then price coefficient preparation, dispatch, stock, hosting and precision.
